title: Continuous Deployment & Automation
description: Set up automatic deploys from your Git repository.

slides.title: What is Continuous Deployment?
slides.content:
# Automate Your Deployments

Continuous Deployment (CD) means that every time you push code to a specific branch (e.g., `main`), your site is automatically built and deployed. This eliminates manual steps and ensures your live site is always up‑to‑date.

**Benefits**:
- No risk of forgetting to deploy.
- Immediate feedback for collaborators.
- Easy rollbacks (just revert the commit).

slides.title: Git‑Based Deployment on Netlify
slides.content:
# Netlify Continuous Deployment

1. Push your code to GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket.
2. In Netlify, choose "New site from Git".
3. Authorize and select your repository.
4. Configure build settings:
   - Build command: `npm run build`
   - Publish directory: `dist`
5. Click "Deploy site".

Now, every `git push` to the main branch will trigger a new deployment. Netlify also gives you preview deployments for pull requests, so you can see changes before merging.

slides.title: GitHub Actions Example
slides.content:
If you prefer more control, you can use GitHub Actions to deploy to any host. Here's a simple workflow for deploying to GitHub Pages:

```yaml
name: Deploy to GitHub Pages

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v3
        with:
          node-version: 18
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run build
      - uses: peaceiris/actions-gh-pages@v3
        with:
          github_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          publish_dir: ./dist
```

This workflow builds the app and pushes the `dist` folder to the `gh-pages` branch, which GitHub Pages serves.

quizData.question: What is the main advantage of continuous deployment?

options.text: It automatically deploys the latest code on every push
It replaces the need for testing

quizData.explanation: Continuous deployment automates the deployment process, so the latest changes are always live without manual intervention.
